newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Lenzing sags after bleeding red ink.
newsitem.headline: Lenzing sags after bleeding red ink.

text.p: Shares in fibre maker Lenzing AG on Thursday took a tumble after the group reported a huge swing into red figures, leading it to scrap its dividend for 1996.
At 0811 GMT, Lenzing was down 17.9 schillings, or 2.56 percent, at 682 schillings. But volume was meagre at just 930 lots traded so far.
Traders said the results sparked "little excitement" as the scrapping of the dividend had already been largely expected when the group released provisional results earlier.

Lenzing forecast market conditions would remain difficult in 1997, after reporting a net loss of 157.4 million schillings in 1996 after a profit of 253.7 million schillings. For 1995 it paid out a 10 schillings per share dividend. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
